title: WPSS/763/2006 of RAKESHA KUMAR MISHRA Vs UTTRANCHAL PARIVAHAN NIGAM and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 763 (SS) of 2006
Rakesh Kumar Mishra ÖÖ.Petitioner
 Versus
Uttaranchal Parivahan Nigam & others ÖÖ.Respondents
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
Mr. M.S. Chauhan, Advocate, present for the
petitioner.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner on delay
condonation application.
3. Delay condonation application (CLMA No.3791 of
2014) is allowed.
4. Delay in filing the restoration application is condoned.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties on the
restoration application.
6. Restoration application (MCC No.172 of 2014) is
allowed.
7. Order dated 21.11.2013 is hereby recalled. Writ
petition is restored to its original number.
8. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner Mr. Mangal
Singh Chauhan, for the petitioner. No counsel is present on
behalf of the respondents to represent the Uttarakhand
Transport Corporation.
9. Briefly, the case of the petitioner is that the petitioner
was a bus conductor in Uttarakhand Transport
Corporation. On 29.05.2001, while the petitioner was on
duty as a conductor in Bus No. UP 29/0126 which was
plying between Tanakpur - Pithoragarh at Maneshwar an
Inspecting team of the Corporation stopped the bus. On

2
inspection, it was found that 301⁄2 passengers who were
sitting in the bus were without ticket. The report which was,
subsequently, filed also reveals that the Conductor i.e. the
petitioner did not open the door of the bus and it was open
with much difficulty. The Inspecting team, thereafter, found
that 30 1⁄2 passengers were not given ticket, although they
had given money to the petitioner i.e. the conductor. The
report also reveals that the petitioner was in an aberrated
state. Disciplinary proceedings were initiated against the
petitioner and a charge-sheet was given to him. The Inquiry
Officer found all the charges against the petitioner to be
proved. Before the Inquiry Committee the petitioner made
his defence as follows:-
 ìAccording to the petitioner on that day he was
not well and, therefore, he had requested his superior
authorities that he may send someone else as Conductor.
His second defence is that since he was not feeling well,
he asked to his fellow conductor Sri U.P. Singh who was
also travelling in the same bus to give tickets to the
passengers and it was U.P. Singh and not the petitioner
who did not give the tickets to the passengers. After
distributing the tickets to the passengers, U.P. Singh
gave the bag to the petitioner and thereafter he was
robbed by a gang of thieves who gave the petitioner some
poisonous food. It was for this reason that he was found
in an aberrated state.î
11. This defence did not, however, help the case of the
petitioner, as it is found in the Inquiry that when the
Inspecting team found that 301⁄2 passengers were not given
tickets, although they have given money to the petitioner,
and petitioner was in an aberrated state, the inspecting
team had asked another conductor, namely, Sri U.P. Singh
who was also travelling in the same bus, to distribute the
tickets to the passengers. It is also on the record that the
petitioner later deposited Rs10, 000/ with the department.

3
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner also submitted that
regarding the same charges, an F.I.R. was also lodged
against the petitioner under Section 409 I.P.C. at Police
Station Kotwali Pithoragarh in which charge sheet was filed
and the petitioner faced the trial. On the strength of the
evidence of the prosecution, the petitioner has not been
found guilty and has been acquitted vide judgement and
order dated 13.10.2004, and since the incident is same, the
order passed in the disciplinary proceedings terminating
the services of the petitioner is bad.
13. This argument of the petitioner is absolutely incorrect,
inasmuch as, in a criminal trial the conviction depends
upon the case of the prosecution which has to be proved
ìbeyond reasonable doubtî, whereas in a departmental
proceeding all which has to be proved is the preponderance
of probabilities. These two proceedings are at entirely
different level and that two cannot be equated.
14. The petitioner has absolutely no case.
15. The writ petition fails and is hereby dismissed. No
order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 21.04.2014
